classification.difficultyReason: Part c requires converting an angle measured from west to an angle from north, then reversing direction using parallel north lines.

spec.description: North at A, with AB extending northeast and a clockwise 54-degree angle from north.
spec.mathematics: The bearing of B from A is 054 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the given 54-degree angle is visible; the formatted bearing is answer content.

answer.worked: The clockwise angle from north at $A$ to $AB$ is $54^{\circ}$. Written as a three-digit bearing, this is $054^{\circ}$.

spec.description: North at B, with BA extending northeast and a clockwise 54-degree angle from north.
spec.mathematics: The bearing of A from B is 054 degrees; the required reverse bearing is 234 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: The given 54-degree angle remains visible; no reverse bearing is printed.

answer.worked:
North lines are parallel. The smaller angle at $A$ is
$$180^{\circ}-54^{\circ}=126^{\circ}\quad\text{(cointerior angles).}$$
The clockwise bearing is
$$360^{\circ}-126^{\circ}=234^{\circ}\quad\text{(angles at a point).}$$

spec.description: North at B and a dashed west cue; BA lies 54 degrees north of west.
spec.mathematics: The smaller angle between north and BA is 90 minus 54, or 36 degrees. The bearing from A to B is 144 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied 54-degree angle and compass cues are visible.

answer.worked:
At $B$, the angle between north and $BA$ is
$$90^{\circ}-54^{\circ}=36^{\circ}.$$
Using parallel north lines, the bearing of $B$ from $A$ is
$$180^{\circ}-36^{\circ}=144^{\circ}\quad\text{(cointerior angles).}$$

answer.worked:
